# The Ruined Tower · Book II, pp. 332–349
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	332
P	A long day's march from Stonetop, a wide, low hill rises from the <b>Flats</b> (page 126).
P	A pile of earth and stone squats atop that hill. Metal spires reach out of the pile, piercing the sky. If you squint, you can see the rubble for what it is: a broken tower, once grand in scale, long ago brought low.
P	Everyone from Stonetop knows about the Ruined Tower and the giant-sized tunnels beneath it. Adventuresome folks sometimes think to explore them. Most of the time, they get spooked and don't go far.
P	But those who've delved deeper have come back with wondrous things. Or never come back at all.
H2	Stormcatcher's tower
HR
P	Before the tower fell, this was home to Stormcatcher, last (?) of the <b>Tempest Lords</b> (page 398). The tower was like the mast of some mighty ship, catching wind and lightning, holding their power in the <b>Storm Orb</b> (page 339), fueling her many magics.
P	For centuries, Stormcatcher's tower stood betwixt the realms of the other <b>Makers</b> (page 264). They would trade with her, and seek her council or her aid. But though the <b>Makers' Roads</b> (page 270) ran to her very gate, she stood apart from them all.
P	Yet she did not live alone. A bustling community grew up around her tower. Laborers, artisans, and scholars. Farmers and domestic help. Soldiers, even. Generations of families. Refugees seeking new homes.
P	Ambassadors and outcasts from the other
P	Makers. Seekers, misfits, and castaways from distant lands.
P	When the Time of Cataclysm came—when the <b>Stone Lords</b>' (page 382) slaves rebelled and unleashed the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412), when the <b>Rime Lords</b>' (page 316) disciples turned savage, when the <b>Forge Lords</b>' (page 156) cities were buried by ash and war—Stormcatcher's tower endured. A bastion of civilization.
P	An island of safety. A refuge.
P	It could not last. Cultists of <b>Og'molok</b> <b>the Faceless Horde</b> (page 349) swarmed the ramparts, driving the defenders back.
P	Og'molok itself burst forth from below as a wave of skittering horrors.
P	Stormcatcher unleashed a mighty spell that turned the attackers into glass. But that same spell shattered the Storm Orb. It laid waste to the tower and broke a stretch of the Makers' Roads. It wrought Stormcatcher's doom.
P	Many of the tower's residents fled through a <b>portal</b> (page 306) beneath the tower. But most were slaughtered by the attackers, or vitrified along with them, or caught in the Storm Orb's explosion. A slim few survivors remained and tried to rebuild, but they soon fell prey to the horrors now loose upon the world.
P	In the centuries since, many have tried to claim the ruin, or plunder its treasures and its secrets. But all have failed, for one reason or another.
P	And the Ruined Tower remains.

H2	Lore
HR
P	<b>Everyone from Stonetop knows:</b>
B	Where the tower is
B	About the giant-sized tunnels below
B	That some brave (foolish) folk have explored them, and found terrible and wondrous things
P	<b>One might know:</b>
B	A tale or two about folks who've explored here and what they found
B	Details about the ruins above ground, or some of the upper tunnels
B	That the tower is a ruin of the Tempest Lords
B	That it was the last of the Makers' strongholds to fall
B	That pieces of the tower can be found strewn all around the Flats
B	That the outer ruins, the tower itself, and the upper tunnels have all been heavily looted, but still yield the occasional trinket
P	<b>Very few know:</b>
B	Stormcatcher's story
B	Her relationship with the other Makers
B	How exactly the tower fell
B	Reliable details about the depths
B	Anything at all about Og'molok, the Faceless Horde

Q	What marvel is said to lie below the Ruined Tower? From whom did you hear such tales?

H2	Hooks
B	Bandits squat in the ruins, and find an artifact that makes them extra dangerous.
B	A sorcerer is raising her demonic child in the tower's depths.
B	A drunk wanderer claims to have explored the depths, but his friends didn't make it out.
B	A southern scholar plans to delve the tower and seeks local help.
B	Frequent earthquakes coincide with terrible nightmares, especially for those touched by violence. The nightmares feature the tower, its fall, or the tunnels below.

H2	Getting there
HR
P	To get there from Stonetop, take the West Road 3-4 hours to the <b>Crossroads</b> (page 270). From there, it's 5-6 hours southwest across the <b>Flats</b> (page 126).
C	It'll take at least a day each way, and a corresponding amount of supplies
C	You'll need to bring light sources (if you intend to explore the tunnels)
C	You need to watch out for <b>nosgalau</b> (page 272) and other <b>dangers</b> (page 130) of the Flats
C	If there have been heavy snows, you must wait until the thaw, or…
C	You'll need snowshoes, and…
C	The way will still be grueling; you risk exhausting yourselves and/or your gear
H2	Areas
B	<b>Overgrown berm</b>, about 15-20' tall, encircling the tower ~3/4 mile out. Huge dressed stones poke out, similar to the <b>Old Wall</b> (page 12).
B	<b>Outer ruins</b> between the berm and the tower. Once a thriving town, now just a jumble of ruins mostly swallowed by the prairie.
B	<b>A shallow crater</b>, stretching ~400' from the tower's northeast edge. Grass/soil/ mud/standing water cover glassy, slaglike bedrock.
B	<b>The tower itself</b>: ~300' across. Northeast third is mostly rubble, but to the south and west a few floors remain, with walls ~200' tall.
B	<b>The upper tunnels</b> start ~100' below the surface. Heavily looted, very haunted, mostly maintained by a ghostly Forge Lord and his <b>patchwork</b> <b>constructs</b> (page 348).
B	<b>The depths</b> are even further down, a warren of chambers, halls, stairs, chutes, and burrows, all in various states of repair. Full of infrastructure, artifacts, experiments, prisons, and vitrified horrors.

H2	Aboveground
HR
P	The Ruined Tower sits atop a wide, low, lightly wooded hill. From a distance, it's just a landmark. As one gets closer, it becomes clear just how massive the tower once was.

B	Smell of ozone, even on a clear day

H3	The Tower itself
P	The base of the tower is ~300' across; rubble and piled-up soil spread out even farther. The south and west sections still stand tall, rising ~200' from the hilltop.
P	<b>Spires:</b> Four <b>metal spires</b> support the tower's walls, one at each cardinal direction:
P	massive, rusted, straining towards the sky.
P	The south and west spires each stretch another 200' or so above the walls (~400' tall total). A length of cable dangles from the tip of the south spire.
P	<b>Rubble:</b> The <b>northeast third</b> of the tower is just rubble, thick walls, and soil piled
P	~30' high, topped with grass and shrubs.
P	The rubble is riddled with trenches, pits, old excavations, buried rooms, burrows.
P	<b>Ground floor:</b> The <b>south and west thirds</b> of the tower are intact at ground level, containing huge vaulted chambers (~40' ceilings), including:
B	A <b>parlor</b> with tall narrow windows. Stylized friezes (faded, vandalized, full of bird nests) show scenes of the <b>Tempest Lord</b> (page 398) empire.
B	The <b>baths</b>, a deep pool full of vile, stagnant water. The walls are busted open, the pipes looted.
B	The <b>great hall</b>, mostly intact, with a giant stone table. The ceiling is enchanted to show the night sky.
P	Human-scale servant passages/rooms parallel the larger chambers and halls.
P	<b>Inlays:</b> Rooms inside the tower once had <b>aetherium inlays</b> (page 341) all along their walls and ceilings, but those were gouged away long ago by looters and <b>thunder drakes</b> (page 135).
P	<b>Main stairwell:</b> A <b>circular shaft</b> at the tower's center, 30' wide. Goes up to the second floor, down ~100' to the upper tunnels.
P	Human-scale stairs spiral along the outer wall, far too small for Makers. Did they <i>fly</i>?
P	<b>Upper floors:</b> The <b>second floor</b> is ~50' up and partly open to the sky, covering the southwest half of the tower. Accessible via the stairwell, holes in ceilings, or climbing the outer walls. A few intact rooms remain, where <b>blue magpies</b> (page 340) stash shinies and build elaborate mosaics.
P	The <b>third and fourth floors</b> are another 40' up each, accessible only via tricky climbs.
P	Unstable, with only a few "rooms," all of which are at least partly open to the air.
P	Magpie nests abound.
HR

H3	Shards of the Storm Orb
P	It was a filigree sphere of <b>aetherium</b> (page 404), maybe 50' across. It floated near the tower, a battery and a focus for tremendous elemental power.
P	Stormcatcher's final spell caused the Orb to explode. Shards were flung across the <b>Flats</b> (page 126), into the tower itself, and deep into the soil—to someday be unearthed by erosion, earthquakes, or burrowing beasts.
P	If the PCs encounter a shard, pick or roll for its size and signs.
P	1d6 size
HR
P	1 Small (Value 0)
P	2 ◇ (Value 1)
P	3-4 ◇◇ (Value 2)
P	5 ◇◇ (<i>cumbersome</i>, Value 2)
P	6 <i>Immobile</i> (Value 3 or more)
P	1d6 signs
HR
P	1 Hums/whines, painfully loud to those who can sense spirits
P	2 Vibrations make odd patterns in soil, prevent growth
P	3 Floats in a pocket of air, loosely covered by rock/soil
P	4 Makes skin tingle, hair stand up
P	5 Nearby soil/stone is blue-white, plants/lichen glow
P	6 Roll twice
P	Shards of the Storm Orb are unstable aetherium (<i>magical</i>, <i>dangerous</i>). If damaged or overloaded, they might explode or violently discharge energy. But they are also etched with arcane runes. Find a big enough piece, or assemble enough smaller ones, and you might unlock some of the Tempest Lords' secrets.
H3	Vitrified remains
P	Stormcatcher's last spell turned anyone it touched into lumps of jagged glass. It was directed at <b>Og'molok</b> (page 349) and the <b>skittering horrors</b> (page 348), but many of the attacking cultists were caught by the spell as well. So were some of the tower's residents.
P	Above ground, vitrified remains are mostly people (attackers or residents), with a few domesticated animals. Most are jagged lumps of black-grey glass, only vaguely recognizable as what they once were, and/ or broken by time or vandalism. These are covered in sharp edges (1d6 damage, <i>messy</i>,
P	1 piercing).
P	A few of these vitrified remains, though, are perfect glass statues, the fear or frenzy of their final moments frozen on their faces (<i>immobile</i>, <i>fragile</i>, Value 3 to the right buyer).
P	<b>Vitrification</b> (page 408) can be reversed, but it's up to you to decide how.

H3	Blue magpie
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>tiny</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>hoarder</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 1; <b>Armor</b> 1 (size)
P	<b>Damage</b> peck d4-2 w/disadvantage (hand)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> smart as a child (at least); can speak Tempest Lord (understood by all)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to amuse/impress its friends
P	• Pretend to be just a dumb bird
P	• Mimic sounds or voices
P	• Mock or trick someone
P	• Steal something
P	• Vanish with a hrummm and reappear nearby (<i>reload</i>)
P	Like big crows with white-and-azure plumage. Their songs are piping and musical, playful and complex, sprinkled with actual voices and other unlikely sounds. A few dozen of them nest in the tower and the surrounding ruins. Smaller mischiefs nest in the Flats.
P	Stormcatcher kept blue magpies as pets, and their descendants have passed down much oral lore. Sneak up on them, and you might overhear magpies telling each other tales that southern scholars would kill to know.
P	Magpies find humans boorish, but fun to mess with, and they have such neat stuff.
P	They love shiny objects, especially glass and fragments of larger things, and spend years making elaborate mosaics or piecing puzzles together.

B	Carefully stacked rubble, plugging holes in walls, blocking off passages

B	Kicked-up dust, catching in your throat, making eyes water
B	The looming menace of a vitrified horror, the skip in your heart before you realize it's just dead glass
B	A thrum or whine, felt in your gut, your teeth, the back of your eyes
B	Wait, haven't we been here before?
HR
H3	Aetherium inlays
P	The four <b>metal spires</b> (page 337) extend down through the bedrock. They run through a number of underground rooms and passages, as freestanding pillars or embedded in walls.
P	Most rooms in and below the tower bear <b>aetherium</b> (page 404) inlays, spreading out from the metal spires. The inlays distribute power and anchor certain spells. Or at least, they used to.
P	The aetherium has been stripped from most of the upper tunnels, either carefully salvaged by <b>patchwork constructs</b> (page 348) or gouged out by looters. More inlays survive in the depths, but even there, many have been marred by <b>star-moles</b> (page 347) or the claws of <b>skittering horrors</b> (page 348), or burnt out and reduced to crumbly chalk.
P	Where intact, inlays glow and pulse in response to winds above ground. When lightning strikes a spire, the aetherium flashes a bright blue-white. Some inlays are stable, but others are erratic and prone to discharge (1d8 damage, <i>forceful</i>, maybe <i>loud</i>).
PAGE	342
HR
H3	Sites
B	<b>Central chamber</b> at the base of the <b>main stairwell</b> (page 337). Big, wellkept, drains in floor, multiple exits.
B	<b>Forge</b> and nearby rooms, haunted by <b>Ferocedes</b> (page 347), packed with tools/parts and constructs in various states of repair.
B	<b>Aetherium crucible</b>, near the forge. Dusty, unused, broken beyond Ferocedes's ability to fix with what's currently available to him.
B	<b>Barracks</b> for soldiers who guarded the <b>Portal</b> (next column). Haunted by evacuees who hid and died there.
B	<b>Latrine</b> near the barracks, with rattling, moaning, clanging pipes and still-working (!) showers.
B	<b>Large chamber</b>, out of the way, the entrance blocked by piled stones. Packed full of vitrified horrors by Ferocedes's constructs.
B	<b>Frozen room</b>, a chokepoint filled with <b>dark ice</b> (page 322), encasing dozens of <b>skittering horrors</b> (page 348) and an <b>Ustrina</b> (page 464) who served as Stormcatcher's steward.
B	<b>Oubliette</b>, a dead-end hall with multiple cells/vaults. Each holds or held a dangerous artifact or entity in stasis. Some are torn open. The rest are guarded by wards, devices, constructs, magic.
B	<b>Bottommost chamber</b>, 400' across, partly flooded. Holds the feet of all four spires, a massive toroidal coil, hundreds of <b>vitrified horrors</b> (page 346), and the trapped manifestation of <b>Og'molok, the Faceless Horde</b> (page 349).
H3	The Portal
P	In the upper tunnels, one can find a pair of double-doors: locked and warded, barricaded from within, with countless gouges clawed across their surface.
P	Beyond those doors: an austere room with a dozen vitrified people, blown-out <b>lightning sconces</b> (page 346), a makerglass window to the next room, and yet another locked door.
P	Beyond that: a once-stately sitting room (the furniture used for the barricade), a few more vitrified evacuees. Another door, this one ajar.
P	One last room. The far wall is a solid white slab, etched with a magic circle. It's a <b>portal</b> (page 306), connected to those in the <b>Labyrinth</b> (page 242), <b>Three Coven Lake</b> (page 438), <b>Vor Svetelik</b> (page 468), and so forth. It is fully functional, and can be used via <b>Opening the Way</b> (page 517).
P	Layers of wards are etched in the floor, directed towards the portal, guarding against things coming out.

H3	Wonders
P	Stormcatcher kept many experiments, curiosities, and dangerous phenomena.
P	Pick 1, roll 1d12, or make up your own.
P	1d12 wonder
P	1 A fountain, its hidden pumps powered by aetherium.
P	2 Nexus of pipes, pumps, boilers. By a stairwell, kept up by <b>patchwork</b> <b>constructs</b> (page 348).
P	3 Deep pit, smooth walls, a <b>jellied</b> <b>horror</b> (page 92) trapped below.
P	Used as a midden pit.
P	4 A huge stone slab, with fittings that make hot, steady flame on demand.
P	5 Room full of plants (<i>exotic</i>, <i>useful</i>, <i>valuable</i>, <i>dangerous</i>). Lit by a makerglass sun, watered by pipes, tended by a fertility spirit.
P	6 Huge orrery. Bits are melted, fused, burnt out; "stars" stuck in a potent cosmic alignment.
P	7 Knee-high dust, shapes itself into whatever an occupant thinks of.
P	Crumbles if removed from room.
P	8 Freestanding arch. Pass through and you vanish. Exit ~5 seconds later, seems instantaneous to you.
P	9 Tight-packed aetherium inlays.
P	Hazy images show what anyone in the room is about to do.
P	10 Sliding tiles in walls/ceiling/floor change gravity's direction and/or intensity in the room.

P	12 Black lightning crackles between two prongs, ~3' apart. Fine glass dust all around. A <b>vitrifying bolt</b> (page 408), just barely contained.

H3	Dangers
P	<b>The environment</b>
B	Getting lost in the maze of tunnels
B	Torches running low, time passing faster than you think
B	<b>Unstable construction</b> (page 390), caused by cataclysm, time, earthquakes, excavation, star-moles
B	Open stairwells, worn-smooth stairs, a lack of railings, a nasty fall
B	The exhausting trudge back up hundreds of stairs
B	Floors wet from rain, snow melt, or leaky pipes, slick and/or muddy
B	Weird growths/bugs: filling the air, shrieking if disturbed, absorbing raw power, spitting it back out
B	Earthquakes or tremors, even worse down here than up above
HR
P	<b>Ancient wonders</b>
B	Damaged <b>aetherium inlays</b> (page 341), erratic and unstable (1d8 damage, <i>forceful</i>, maybe <i>loud</i>)
B	Pressurized pipes, spewing steam or scalding water if ruptured (1d8 damage, <i>area</i>)
B	Metal bulkheads, rigged to drop and contain runaway spells/experiments/ prisoners
B	Raw chemics, neatly stowed, spilled, seeping
B	Machines, running erratically, fully able to rend flesh and bone
B	Broken laws of reality, and whatever that does to mind/body/soul
B	<b>Radiation</b> (page 407), hopefully contained, probably not
B	<b>Smoke, fire, and heat</b> (page 166) in the haunted forge
B	<b>Perilous stone</b> (page 391): stolen, imported, borrowed, replicated <b>Corruption, as one goes deeper</b>
B	<b>Disquiet and unease</b> (page 428), especially near masses of vitrified horrors
B	<b>Whispers and visions</b> (page 428), coming from the horrors, or from below, or from everywhere at once
B	<b>Unnatural phenomena</b> (page 429), as one approaches the bottommost chamber and what remains of <b>Og'molok</b> (page 349).

H3	Vitrified horrors
P	<b>Skittering horrors</b> (page 348), fused into black, jagged glass by Stormcatcher's last spell. There are more and more as you go deeper. In some places, they clog stairs or passages, making it difficult to squeeze by without your gear or your flesh getting shredded (1d4 to 1d8 damage, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing).

H3	Star-mole
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>hardy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 7; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> caustic spit or blood d6 w/disadvantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> blind; tremorsense; bioluminescent <b>Instinct</b> to lure predators into traps
P	• Soften stone with its spit, then dig through it
P	• Spurt caustic blood when hurt
P	• Scamper away, hide, act as bait
P	• Trigger a collapse or cave-in Big, naked mole-rats, like 5' long, with saggy skin, glowing freckles, and clusters of wriggling feelers on their noses. They eat vermin and fungus that grow near leaking pipes. They also tunnel through bedrock, collapse passages, and expose sealed-off rooms.
P	Every so often, they wake a <b>skittering</b> <b>horror</b> (page 348) from its torpor. This spells doom for the colony, unless they can trap it or cut off access to the nest. They'll treat the PCs as a similar threat.
ICON	icons/beast-large.svg
H3	Ferocedes Ogran, ghostly
H3	Forge Lord
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>undead</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>obsessive</i>, <i>absentminded</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 23; <b>Armor</b> 4 (metal, amorphous)
P	<b>Damage</b> pummel d12+3 (<i>close</i>, <i>reach</i>, <i>forceful</i>) or barrage of metal d10+1
P	(<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>messy</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>reload</i>,
P	1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to his forge, and can't venture far from it; speaks Tempest Lord (understood by all)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to preserve/restore the tower, to ignore harsh truths
P	• Manifest a cloud of ember and ash, a voice of crackling flame
P	• Ask what they've brought him, if that one task is done yet, etc.
P	• Fail to understand their speech
P	• Grow annoyed, angry, violent
P	• Manipulate metal, telekinetically
P	• Repair metal, or shape it anew
P	• Animate a body formed of metal tools, parts, and scrap
P	In life, he was a brilliant but awkward Maker. Rivals sabotaged him, and he left his people in shame. Stormcatcher took him in, trusted him, gave him purpose—and for that, Ferocedes was rabidly loyal.
P	Loyal unto death, and beyond.
P	He died without noticing it. He had no time to treat the wounds he had suffered.
P	Stormcatcher needed his skills. Needed his creations. Needed him.
P	So Ferocedes was already a ghost when Stormcatcher cast her final spell. And in the centuries since, he has fixated on his task: to reclaim, rebuild, and repair, little by little, with what tools he has, and preserve the memory of his friend.

H3	Patchwork construct
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 14; <b>Armor</b> 3 (metal)
P	<b>Damage</b> tool at hand d8 (<i>hand</i> or <i>close</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> must recharge every few days; dog-like intellect; blind; tremorsense <b>Instinct</b> to complete its given task
P	• Size up an obstacle or task
P	• Reveal/use a tool, feature, or attachment for its current task
P	• Plod away, raise the alarm
P	Ferocedes once had dozens of constructs to defend and maintain the tower. But the years have not been kind. Only ten or so remain, and one or two are usually offline for modifications or repairs.
P	Each one has an aetherium core (◇ <i>magical</i>, <i>fragile</i>, Value 2 to the right buyer).
P	Ferocedes can repair minor damage to a core, and/or install it in a new body, but he can't make new ones without the <b>aetherium crucible</b> (page 405).
P	Each construct is generally humanoid, though most lack a "head" and all are made of mismatched parts. Pick or roll a current task for each. Consider picking or rolling for an attribute (page 167) and adjusting its stat block accordingly.

P	1 Patrolling/guarding/defending

P	3 Plumbing/other delicate work
P	4 Sweeping/cleaning/pest control
P	5 Hauling/storing/reorganizing
P	6 Seeking/retrieving/inspecting

P	• Savage a fallen foe 6 feet long, with segmented bodies and too many legs. Scythe-like forelimbs. Feathery antennae that caress the air and quiver when they sense prey. No eyes, just red crystal pulsing within its skull. No mouth, for it never eats and lives on hate and malice.
PAGE	349
P	Each is a manifestation of Og'molok's cruel will. Born of blood, given shape, sent skittering up to slaughter. And slaughter they did, until Stormcatcher's final spell turned them all into jagged lumps of glass.
P	Or, almost all of them. A few dozen avoided the vitrifying spell. They linger on, in a state of torpor until they sense a living, feeling being. Then they wake. Then they hunt. Then they slaughter once more.
HR
ICON	icons/threat.svg
H3	Og'molok, the Faceless Horde
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to revel in slaughter, pain, and terror
P	<b>Themes</b> cruelty/torture/violence and destruction/chaos/ruin
P	• Send terrible dreams/visions to those touched by violence
P	• Urge bloodshed, cruelty, rage
P	• Shake the earth in a fit
P	In the <b>bottommost chamber</b> (page 342) of the Ruined Tower is a cone of jagged black glass, a pile of vitrified horrors that reaches almost to the ceiling. This is where Og'molok burst into the world as a fountain of blood, coalescing into a skittering swarm. This is where it met its doom, fused into a pillar of <b>red crystal</b> (page 424), encased in a pile of slag.
P	Og'molok, of course, is not truly dead. Just bound, neutered, diminished. It still corrupts the lowest levels beneath the tower, still calls to those who might hear. It is trapped, and it cannot escape. Not yet. Not without help.
C	Someone sets out to free it
C	They learn how to release it from its <b>vitrified</b> state (see page 408)
C	They acquire what they need
C	They begin the process
C	<b>Impending doom</b>: Og'molok and its swarm are loosed upon the world
